institution: Uttar Pradesh University of Medical Sciences, Saifai (Department of Microbiology)
period: Not stated in the document; the UPUMS Microbiology notice list titles it 'Antibiogram 2023' (notice dated 1 April 2023; PDF created 2 November 2023, uploaded April 2024)
citation: Department of Microbiology, Uttar Pradesh University of Medical Sciences. Antibiogram 2023 (compilers Dr Keshav et al.; approver Dr R K Verma). Saifai, Etawah: UPUMS; 2023.
reporting: Percent susceptible shown as bar charts with printed data labels, by specimen (urine, blood, sputum, pus and exudates, body fluids) and organism or organism group, hospital-wide; no isolate numbers per chart. Organism distribution charts by OPD, ward and ICU per specimen (data labels on the urine and body fluid charts only). AST method and breakpoint standard not stated.

verification.note: Every recorded value is a printed data label: read from the pages rendered at scale 2 (charts zoomed at scale 3 to 3.5 where needed) and compared with the data labels in the PDF text layer in left-to-right order (all 10 charts agree; the drug names on the x axes are not in the text layer and were read from the images, and the number of drug labels matched the number of bars in every chart). Organism counts on p3 and p19 were read from the zoomed charts; p19 labels missing from the text layer were read from the image.

notes: Earlier UPUMS Saifai hospital antibiogram (23 pages, all charts). The document states no data period; the year is taken from the institution's own title for it on the Microbiology notice list ('Antibiogram 2023'), and no end month is given. Per specimen it gives samples received from ICU, OPD and wards (urine 586/471/507; blood 1839/9/426; sputum 164/90/325; pus 59/127/165; body fluids 1355 by fluid type), an organism distribution chart by setting, and percent-susceptible bar charts that are hospital-wide. Only charts for a single organism group with printed data labels are recorded (10 charts): urine Klebsiella; blood, pus and body fluid Acinetobacter, Citrobacter and Pseudomonas. Charts that pool different genera (E. coli with Proteus, Klebsiella with Enterobacter, Enterococcus with CoNS, Acinetobacter with Pseudomonas, and mixed Gram-positive groups) are left out because no organism key represents them and their members differ in intrinsic resistance (for example, the pus E. coli and Proteus chart prints polymyxin B 84.6%, which the Proteus isolates alone could explain). The six sputum charts have no data labels and are left out. Organism counts are recorded from the labelled urine (p3) and body fluid (p19) distribution charts only; the blood, sputum and pus distribution charts have no labels, so the counts cover only part of the isolates. Several printed figures are implausible for the organism (for example ampicillin 35% for blood Citrobacter and 85.7% for blood Klebsiella with Enterobacter); they are recorded as printed where kept, and the build marks intrinsic-resistance pairs. Data quality of this edition is lower than the 2024 edition (UPUMS_SAIFAI_2024), which supersedes it. Page numbers are PDF pages.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 97 cells (10 charts) and all 45 organism counts re-read against the page images (scale 2.2, charts zoomed at scale 4), each value read before comparing; 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected.

The 6 intrinsic cells (Citrobacter ampicillin 35% blood and 12.5% pus; Acinetobacter pus ampicillin 35.6% and amoxicillin-clavulanate 23.6%, body fluid ampicillin 33.3% and chloramphenicol 80%) and the caution cell (body fluid Citrobacter chart with two bars labelled Amikacin, 66.6% and 67%) are printed as recorded; the body fluid Staphylococcus counts (0, 2, 6) are rightly left out.
